newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Rainstorm no big impact on Malaysia cocoa - growers.
newsitem.headline: Rainstorm no big impact on Malaysia cocoa - growers.

text.p: Malaysian cocoa growers said on Monday that a rainstorm which lashed the eastern state of Sabah last week was not expected to have a major impact on national production of the crop.

Sabah produces about 80 percent of Malaysia's cocoa but the storm's major hit was on Keningau, a tiny logging town which contributes only 2,500 tonnes or 2.0 percent of national cocoa production, the growers said.
"It's quite difficult to say yet what the (storm's) exact impact will be, but I don't think it will be much (on cocoa)," a Sabah cocoa grower told Reuters by telephone.
The Malaysian Cocoa Board has estimated production in 1996 to be 122,000 tonnes against 131,000 in 1995.
Tropical storm Greg created floods and destroyed property, killing 163 people and leaving some 104 missing.
Another Sabah-based grower said Tenom, a district which neighbours Keningau and produces nearly a third of Sabah's cocoa output, was also "slightly affected" by the storm.
"All in all, the production forecast for 1996 should hold," said the grower. Estimates on the damage were not available.

Floods and heavy rains in Sabah since late 1995 have destroyed the first two cocoa harvests between April and June and July and September this year, growers told Reuters in a poll made early this month.

The growers, who were almost resigned to a bad final crop between October and December, said a slowdown in rains and fresh flowering on cocoa trees in the last couple of months had saved the year-end harvest from being worse.
